why: An app shell is composition, not a block: Quill ships sidebar-nav, dashboard and mail-shell as the parts. The two implementations share only the word (253 lines on next/navigation vs a 130-line mobile shell).
Approval and work queues are product-domain objects; Quill ships the parts they compose (data-table, list-detail, activity-feed), not the domain.
Domain-specific to one product (an agent crew rail and a 1088-line map); one app's feature is not a pattern.
Both are thin wrappers over next/link (58 and 16 lines); link colour and hover already come from the accent tokens, so there is nothing for a block to add.
Brand marks and company logos are per-app assets by definition; Quill's own mark is not a consumer component.
Same as logo: a brand icon set belongs to the app that owns the brand.
